segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Looking up, he saw rich people putting their gifts into the treasury.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He also saw a needy widow putting in two small copper coins,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “In truth I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for all of these added to the gifts out of their surplus, but she, out of her need, put in everything she had to live on.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As some were speaking about the temple, how it was adorned with beautiful stones and dedicated offerings, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “As for these things you are looking at, days will come when not a stone will be left on a stone that will not be torn down.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, when then will these things be, and what will be the sign when they are about to happen?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not go after them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And when you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified; for these things must happen first, but the end will not come at once.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: there will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and plagues, and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to the synagogues and prisons, and you will be led away before kings and governors for the sake of my name.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It will lead to your giving testimony.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So settle it in your hearts not to rehearse your defense beforehand,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for I myself will give you a mouth and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to withstand or contradict.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you will be hated by everyone because of my name.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet not a single hair of your head will perish.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: By your endurance gain your lives.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has drawn near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, those inside the city must get out, and those in the countryside must not enter it,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: because these are days of retribution, so that all that is written may be fulfilled.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days! For there will be great distress on the land and wrath against this people,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth nations in anguish, at a loss before the roar of the sea and its surging,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: people fainting from fear and foreboding at what is coming upon the inhabited world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When these things begin to happen, stand up straight and lift your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he told them a parable:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When they are already putting out leaves, you see it and know for yourselves that summer is already near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until everything has happened.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But be on your guard, or your hearts may be weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the worries of daily life, and that day may come upon you suddenly

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: like a trap. For it will come upon all who live on the face of the whole earth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But stay awake at all times, praying that you may have the strength to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: During the days he was teaching in the temple, but at night he would go out and spend the night on the hill called the Mount of Olives.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all the people would come to him early in the morning in the temple to listen to him.

notes.note: The lepton was the smallest coin in circulation in Judea, a tiny fraction of a labourer's daily wage. Two of them would buy almost nothing. The point of the scene is that they were all she had.

The Greek is simply ‘I am’ (egō eimi). Most translations supply ‘he’ and take it as a claim to be the Messiah, as the parallel in Matthew 24:5 spells out. Some hear an echo of God's self-declaration in the Greek Scriptures; that is possible but cannot be shown.

One Greek word, ethnos, lies behind ‘nation’ here, ‘all the nations’ and ‘Gentiles’ in verse 24, and ‘nations’ in verse 25. It means a people; in the plural it was also the ordinary Jewish term for the non-Jewish peoples. English translations regularly divide it by sense in this way, but in verse 24 the nations to which captives are taken and the Gentiles who trample Jerusalem are the same word.

notes.phrase: It will lead to your giving testimony
notes.traditional: it shall turn to you for a testimony
notes.note: The Greek says literally ‘it will turn out for you into testimony’. Most interpreters take this to mean that arrest and trial will become the disciples' occasion to bear witness, and the translation follows that view. It could also mean that the outcome will stand as testimony in the disciples' favour.

notes.traditional: you will gain your lives / possess ye your souls
notes.note: The text translated here has a command, ‘gain’; many manuscripts have a future, ‘you will gain’, and many English versions render it as a promise. The word translated ‘lives’ (psychē) is traditionally ‘souls’. It means a person's life or self, and here it refers to a life that survives even the death foretold in verse 16.

Roman armies besieged Jerusalem and destroyed the city and its temple in AD 70. Where Mark 13:14 and Matthew 24:15 speak of ‘the abomination of desolation’, Luke speaks plainly of armies and keeps the word ‘desolation’.

The Greek word means the exacting of justice or punishment, without the note of personal spite that ‘vengeance’ can carry in modern English. The phrase echoes the Greek Old Testament, where the prophets speak of the days of God's punishment (for example Hosea 9:7). Many versions still use ‘vengeance’.

notes.traditional: in the land / upon the earth
notes.note: The Greek word means both ‘land’ and ‘earth’, and translations are divided here. Because the next phrase speaks of ‘this people’ and the subject is Jerusalem and Judea, the land of Israel is the more likely meaning. In verse 25, where it is set against sun, moon and stars, the same word is rendered ‘earth’.

This is not the usual word for ‘world’ (kosmos) but oikoumenē, the inhabited earth, the world of human society. In ordinary usage it often meant in practice the Roman world, as in Luke 2:1. Most translations render it simply ‘the world’.

notes.traditional: the powers of heaven / of the heavens
notes.note: The Greek is plural, and the plural is kept. The phrase draws on the language of the prophets (compare Isaiah 34:4) and refers to the heavenly host: sun, moon and stars, which ancient readers commonly associated with heavenly beings. Their shaking signals the undoing of the established order of the cosmos.

The natural sense of the Greek is the people alive at the time of speaking, and many scholars take it so, referring ‘everything’ chiefly to the fall of Jerusalem. Others have understood it as the generation that sees the final signs, or more broadly as the Jewish people or humankind. The meaning is disputed, and the translation leaves the wording as it stands.

notes.traditional: For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell
notes.note: Manuscripts differ on where the sentence divides. In the text translated here, ‘like a trap’ completes verse 34: the day springs on the unwary like a trap. In many manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, the words begin the next sentence: ‘for like a trap it will come upon all’.

candidates.reason: Jesus' formula recurs across all four Gospels, and translators divide between 'Truly' and 'Amen'; Luke also alternates it with ἀληθῶς (v. 3), which the English should keep distinct.
The choice between 'soul', 'life' and 'self' recurs throughout the New Testament, and inconsistent handling would mislead readers about what is being saved or lost.
It is distinct from κόσμος and γῆ and recurs in Luke-Acts, Hebrews and Revelation; a fixed rendering would keep it from collapsing into 'world' or 'earth'.
It is frequent in Paul, James and Revelation, and translations vary between 'patience', 'endurance', 'perseverance' and 'steadfastness'.
It is a key term in Paul and Hebrews; 'redemption', 'liberation', 'deliverance' and 'release' are all defensible and should not vary by chapter.
